utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case IT-94-1-PT, the Prosecutor against Dusko Tadic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Currently, there are four motions before the Trial Chamber in this case, determination of three of which, those dealing with the form of the indictment, the principle of non-bis-in-idem and a request for protective measures for a witness, have been reserved to today. The fourth motion, which relates to the broadcasting of the Tribunal's proceedings, remains pending. The unanimous decision of the Trial Chamber on each of these three Motions is handed down today. I shall now address each of these three Motions separately. The first Motion is a Motion filed by the Defence on 23rd June 1995 challenging the form of the indictment for being too vague and for charging offences as concurrent offences under the Statute, and not in the alternative. Following the amendment of the indictment on September 1st 1995, a second Motion was filed on September 4th 1995. Both Motions seek to have the indictment dismissed or, alternatively, an order that the Prosecutor further amend the indictment to rectify the alleged defects. The Prosecutor filed two Responses to those Motions, on July 7th and September 26th 1995 respectively, asserting that the indictment is not defective, that the procedures of this Tribunal as to the disclosure of evidence provide all necessary information to the accused to enable him to prepare a proper defence and that the offences may be properly charged concurrently. The hearing of the Motion was postponed pending the outcome of the interlocutory appeal on jurisdiction filed by the Defence and was eventually heard in open session on October 24th 1995. The Order of the Trial Chamber in this matter is as follows: Having considered the written and oral submissions of the parties, the Trial Chamber, pursuant to Rule 72 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence: (1) grants the Motion in so far as it relates to paragraph 4 of the indictment as amended on September 1st 1995; (2) grants leave to the Prosecutor to amend paragraph 4 of the indictment within 30 days of delivery of this Decision; and (3) dismisses the Motion in all other respects. The second Motion pending before the Trial Chamber was also filed by the Defence on June 23rd 1995. In it, the Defence asserted that the proceedings before the Trial Chamber should be dismissed as constituting a breach of the principle of non-bis-in-idem or, as it sometimes known, double jeopardy, based on the existence of proceedings against the accused in the Federal Republic of Germany. These proceedings before the Tribunal commenced, and the accused is present before us today, as a consequence of the deferral by the Federal Republic of Germany of its proceedings to this Tribunal pursuant to a formal request for a deferral issued by the Trial Chamber on November 8th 1994. Again, a second Motion was filed on September 4th 1995, following the amendment of the indictment, and on July 7th and September 26th 1995 the Prosecutor filed Responses contesting the Motion. Argument was heard on this Motion, together with the Motion relating to the form of the indictment, on October 24th 1995. At that hearing, leave was given to the Defence to file additional information concerning the nature of proceedings in the Federal Republic of Germany. That information was filed on October 30th 1995 and the Prosecutor responded on November 1st 1995. The Order of the Trial Chamber in this matter is as follows: Having considered the written and oral submissions of the parties, the Trial Chamber, pursuant to Rule 72 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, dismisses the Motion and denies the relief sought by the Defence in its Motion on Ne-Bis-in-Idem. The third and final Motion is one filed by the Prosecutor on July 31st 1995 seeking protective measures for a witness referred to by the letter "L". The Motion contained 12 separate prayers for relief. On September 28th 1995 the Defence filed its Response objecting in part and agreeing in part to the protective measures sought. On October 6th 1995 the Prosecutor filed a Reply, which took into account the decision of August 10th 1995 issued by this Trial Chamber on a previous Motion by the Prosecutor seeking protective measures in respect of other witnesses, and amended the relief sought. At the request of the Prosecutor, and with agreement of the Defence, the Motion was heard in closed session on October 25th 1995. The Order of the Trial Chamber in this matter is as follows: Having considered the written and oral submissions of the parties, the Trial Chamber, pursuant to Rule 75 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, orders as follows: (1) the name, address, whereabouts of, and other identifying data concerning the person given pseudonym L shall not be disclosed to the public or to the media; (2) all hearings to consider the issue of protective measures for witness L shall be in closed session; however, edited recordings and transcripts of these sessions shall be released to the public and to the media after review by the Office of the Prosecutor in consultation with the Victims and Witnesses Unit; (3) the name, address, whereabouts of, and identifying data concerning witness L shall be sealed and not included in any of the public records of the International Tribunal; (4) to the extent the name, address, whereabouts of, or other identifying data concerning witness L is contained in existing documents of the International Tribunal, the name and other identifying data shall be expunged from those records; (5) documents of the International Tribunal identifying witness L shall not be disclosed to the public or to the media; (6) the testimony of witness L shall be heard in closed session; however, edited recordings and transcripts of the session(s) shall be released to the public and to the media after review by the Office of the Prosecutor in consultation with the Victims and Witnesses Unit. (7) the pseudonym L shall be used whenever referring to this witness in proceedings before the International Tribunal and in discussions among parties to the trial; (8) no identifying data concerning witness L, other than his name and position at the Trnopolje camp, and the time taken for travel by witness L from his residence to the camp, shall be disclosed to Defence counsel or to the accused, and the names, addresses, whereabouts, and other identifying data concerning witness L's relatives shall not be disclosed to the Defence or to the accused. (9) the name of witness L and information relating to the time taken for travel by witness L from his residence to the Trnopolje prison camp shall be disclosed to the Defence not less than 30 days in advance of a firm trial date; (10) the accused, the Defence counsel and their representatives, who are acting pursuant to their instructions or request, shall not disclose the name of witness L, or any other identifying data they may discover concerning witness L, to the public or to the media, except to the limited extent such disclosure to members of the public is necessary to investigate the witness adequately. Any such disclosure shall be made in such a way as to minimise the risk of the witness's name being divulged to the public at large or to the media; (11) the accused, the Defence counsel and their representatives, who are acting pursuant to their instructions or request, shall notify the Office of the Prosecutor of any requested contact with witness L or the relatives of witness L, and the Office the Prosecutor shall make arrangements for such contact as is determined may be necessary; and (12) the public and the media shall not photograph, video record or sketch witness L within the precincts of the International Tribunal. That concludes the reading of the statement regarding these three Decisions. Are there additional matters that need to be brought to the attention of the Tribunal Chamber at this time, Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. If there is nothing else, then the Chamber will stand adjourned until January 16th 1996. (Adjourned until 16th January 1996)
